triggered ability - check log for discard - check if effective attack power of card is is 6 or greater - if yes - create 'might token' in play on player's board. - this can only create 1 might token per turn.

triggered ability - whenever 'the crowd boos you' : create a might token on player's board.

hero-boltyn:

hero-enigma: static ability conditional cost reduction - if  an attack has name 'spectral shield' - reduce the resources required by 1.
hero-gravy-bones:
instant activated ability - cost is 'tap gravy bones' + 'destroy a gold you control'. both halves are real costs, so if there is no gold on the board the ability is unpayable and must stay INERT, not free (same discipline as v2.04). popup: if more than one gold, select which to destroy.

effect ordering matters and the card spells it out - 'draw a card, THEN discard a card'. draw first, then open the discard popup over the new hand, so the card just drawn is a legal discard. a combined 'rummage' that picks the discard before the draw is wrong.

second clause is a PERMISSION, not an effect - 'if a blue card has been put into your graveyard this turn, you may play cards with watery grave from your graveyard.' the condition is already answerable today: the graveyard is turn-stamped, so it is 'any card in grave with _gy === current turn and pitch === 3'. what is NOT answerable is watery grave itself - the card database carries no reminder text for it (i checked all 48 cards that mention it; every one references the keyword and none defines it). so this clause is blocked on a RULING for watery grave, not on parser work. see the no-op blind spot note in CLAUDE.md - barnacle reports tier FULL with watery grave filed as a no-op, which is exactly the mis-filing that hides this.
hero-dorinthea:
triggered ability, once per turn - 'when a weapon you control HITS'. hit is the precise CR 7.5.5 sense: if prevention means no damage is dealt it is NOT a hit and this must not fire. the trainer already needs that distinction for on-hit effects, so reuse it rather than checking 'damage was attempted'.

on trigger - popup: 'attack again with <weapon>?' yes/no (the card says 'you may'). on yes, grant one additional weapon attack with THAT specific weapon this turn - not any weapon, and it does not cost an action point.

this is the same 'extra weapon activation' machinery the flurry token needs. build it once and let both call it. note the once-per-turn cap is on the ABILITY, not on the weapon - two different weapons hitting in one turn still only gets you one extra attack.
hero-iyslander:
NOT A GAP - the one 'unread' clause is 'Essence of Ice', which is a talent/deck-building header exactly like briar's 'Essence of Earth and Lightning', and that one is already ruled as 'a static ability that we do not need to worry about'. it is a correct no-op.

the other two clauses already read. so iyslander is effectively complete and the 1/3 should not be counted against her.

worth acting on at the tool level: the sweep's '32 unread hero clauses' includes at least these two 'Essence of X' header lines, so the real number is smaller. sweep.js could skip a clause that is a bare 'Essence of ...' with no verb - otherwise this pair will keep showing up as work forever.
token-runechant:
already carried as a dedicated counter (rune), and that is the right shape - keep it. the printed text matches what the engine does on the main path: 'when you play an attack action card or activate a weapon attack, destroy this and deal 1 arcane damage to target opposing hero', all of them, mandatorily, each a separate source.

the one real deviation is ORDERING, and it is already known: a runechant created by playing an attack currently pops on that same swing. the trigger is 'when you PLAY an attack action card' - a runechant that does not exist at that moment cannot have triggered. fix is to snapshot the rune count at the instant the attack is played, before that attack's own effects resolve, and pop exactly that many.

because each runechant is its own source, ward / arcane barrier apply per runechant, not once to the total. worth a drill.
token-frostbite:
carried as the frost counter. two clauses, and the second is what keeps it fair: 'cards and abilities cost you an additional {r}' AND 'at the beginning of your end phase OR when you play a card or activate an ability, destroy Frostbite'. so it taxes exactly ONE card and then dies - it is a one-shot tax, not a standing one. an implementation that leaves it up all turn is much stronger than the card.

controller matters: iyslander creates it 'under their control', i.e. it is the OPPONENT's aura and taxes the OPPONENT's costs. this is why it is inert today - the dummy pays no costs and has no action phase. it stays inert until roadmap item 3, and that is honest, but the destroy-on-play half should be built now so it is not forgotten when the dummy starts paying.

needs a 'beginning of end phase' hook, shared with bloodrot pox and frailty.
token-seismic-surge:
'at the beginning of your action phase, destroy this, then the next Guardian attack action card you play this turn costs {r} less to play.'

blocked on a SCHEDULE, not on parsing - the trainer has no 'beginning of action phase' hook. that hook is the deliverable; seismic surge, confidence (start of turn) and the end-phase tokens are all waiting on the same kind of thing.

the discount is narrow and easy to over-build: Guardian only, attack ACTION cards only (not weapon attacks), next one only, that turn only. cost reductions already read the board by name via boardRed, so the discount itself has a home - it is the timing that is missing.

caveat on the '4 mentions in the trainer' signal: per CLAUDE.md at least one of those is inside a refusal message, so treat the count as zero evidence of real handling.
token-courage:
'when you play an attack action card or activate a weapon attack, destroy this and the attack gets +1{p}.'

this is structurally the SAME trigger as runechant - identical trigger clause, different payload (+1 power to the attack instead of 1 arcane damage to the hero). that is the engineering point: put both on one trigger bus keyed on 'attack played or weapon activated', and let each token register its payload. building courage as a second bespoke counter duplicates the thing runechant already got right.

unlike runechant it does not target and cannot be warded - it is a pump on your own attack. it must land before the total is struck, which is the same declaration-time ordering the reveal effects already use.
token-confidence:
'at the start of your turn, destroy this, then the next attack card you play this turn can't be defended by more than 2 non-block cards.'

two pieces of machinery, one of which already exists. the defender limit IS dominate's machinery with a different number - dominate limits the defender to 1 card from hand, this limits to 2 non-block cards. generalise the existing limit into (count, qualifier) rather than adding a parallel field.

read the qualifier carefully: 'non-block cards', not 'non-equipment'. equipment blocking is unaffected, and so is anything the rules count as a block card. this is narrower than defLt2, which counts non-equipment hand blockers - do not reuse defLt2 for it.

needs the 'start of your turn' schedule. note it destroys itself at start of turn whether or not you then play an attack, so it is use-it-or-lose-it.
token-fealty:
'**Instant** - Destroy this: The next card you play this turn is Draconic. At the beginning of your end phase, if you haven't created a Fealty token or played a Dragonic card this turn, destroy this.'

FLAG FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THIS: the printed text says 'Dragonic' in the second sentence and 'Draconic' in the first. that is a real typo on the real card, and it means a parser keyed on /draconic/ will read the grant and silently miss the end-phase condition. match both spellings, and put a comment on it so nobody 'fixes' it later.

the effect is a TYPE GRANT on the next card you play this turn - it makes that card Draconic, which is what turns on fai's chain-link cost reduction and anything else keyed on the type. so it needs a pending type-override slot, not a power/cost buff.

the end-phase clause is a turn-history predicate: 'created a fealty this turn OR played a draconic this turn'. hist already carries per-turn data, so this is a field on it rather than new plumbing.
token-flurry:
'when you activate a weapon attack, destroy this and you may attack with the weapon twice this turn.'

same extra-weapon-attack machinery as dorinthea's hero ability - build it once, call it from both. 'you may' means a popup, and 'twice this turn' is a cap, not a grant of two extra swings: it sets the weapon's allowed attacks for the turn to 2 total.

ordering trap: the trigger is on ACTIVATE, so it fires and destroys itself before the first attack resolves. the second attack is available even if the first one is fully blocked or fizzles.
token-bloodrot-pox:
'at the beginning of your end phase, destroy Bloodrot Pox, then it deals 2 damage to you unless you pay {r}{r}{r}.'

this is a textbook `pay` prompt spec and that variant has existed since v2.17 - so it is no longer blocked on machinery, it just needs writing. spec: tag 'pay', side = the token's controller (NOT always side 0 - this is one of the cards that proves prompts must be addressed to a side), cost {r}{r}{r}, ops = 2 damage to that side's hero on DECLINE.

mind the polarity: the payload fires when you DON'T pay. that is inverted from most pay prompts, where paying buys the effect. get it backwards and the token becomes a reward.

also mind the end phase: resources are lost at end of turn (CR 4.4.3e), so by the time this resolves the controller may have nothing to pay with. that is correct and brutal - it is why the card is a threat - but it means the prompt has to read what they can actually spend at that moment, which is what avail is for.
token-frailty:
'your attack action cards played FROM ARSENAL and weapon attacks have -1{p}. at the beginning of your end phase destroy Frailty.'

the narrowness is the whole card and it is very easy to over-build: it is NOT -1 to all your attacks. it hits exactly two things - attack action cards played from the arsenal, and weapon attacks. an attack action played from hand is untouched. an implementation that just subtracts 1 from every attack makes this token far stronger than it is.

the engine already knows where a card was played from (pending.from is 'arsenal' / 'hand'), so the condition is readable today - this is a real, buildable one.

like frostbite it dies at the beginning of the end phase, so it taxes exactly one turn.
token-graphene-chelicera:
the odd one out: every other token in this list is an Aura, this one is a WEAPON - types are [Assassin, Token, Weapon, Dagger, 1H]. so it does not go on the board, it needs a weapon zone slot, and creating it when both weapon slots are full has to have a defined answer. that is the engine question here, and it is different from every other token.

kayo is the reason this matters more than it looks - he has only 1 weapon zone.

its own text is three things: stealth (a qualifier, already ruled), a once-per-turn {r} attack activation, and 'when this attacks a marked hero, the attack gets go again' - which needs the marked check arakni's hero ability already needs. shares machinery with hero-arakni-web-of-deceit.
fail-look-tuff-1:
'when this attacks, it gets -1{p} unless you pay {r}.' the ruling is already recorded (card-look-tuff-1) so this is build work, not a rules question.

the thing that makes it UNFAIR today is the DEFAULT. an 'unless you pay' clause means NOT paying is the baseline - the card is priced as a -1 attack that you may buy back up to full. right now the drawback is skipped entirely, so every look tuff swings at full power for free. so: apply the -1 FIRST, and let paying remove it. never the other way round.

every path that is not an explicit successful payment must land on -1: prompt declined, prompt skipped, player has no resource, player cancels the pitch, prompt machinery errors. if in doubt, -1.

timing: the trigger is 'when this attacks', so the prompt has to resolve BEFORE the attack total is struck, or the number on screen is wrong even when the engine is right. that is the declaration-time path CLAUDE.md already describes for reveal / revPitch - look tuff belongs on it, not in resolveStack.

the pay prompt variant has existed since v2.17, so nothing here is blocked on machinery. spec: tag 'pay', side 0, cost {r}, ops = remove the -1. note it is the INVERSE polarity of bloodrot pox (there the payload fires when you DON'T pay) - worth a drill on each so the two do not get copy-pasted into each other.
fail-hero-lyath-goldmane:
THIS IS THE BIGGEST ONE IN THE POOL AND IT IS NOT RULED YET - flagging it as such rather than guessing.

'The base {p} and {d} of cards you control are halved, rounded up.' right now this is skipped completely, which means lyath plays his entire deck at DOUBLE the stats he is supposed to have, on both offence and defence, in every game. every other sev-3 entry is one card; this one is a whole hero. it is also the reason he is allowed 5 intellect when every other hero has 4 - the halving IS the price of that extra card, and the sim is currently handing him the card without the price. i played 20 games with him for this pass and he is not remotely the same hero the card describes.

the part that needs care is ORDER OF OPERATIONS, and it is what 'Displayed total is wrong' is pointing at. it says BASE {p} and {d}. so: halve the printed base first, round up, and only THEN apply pumps, buffs and boosts. a base 3 attack with +2{p} is 2+2 = 4. it is NOT ceil(5/2) = 3. getting this backwards makes his pump cards look worthless and will read as 'the buffs are broken'.

rounding is up, so it never reaches 0: base 1 -> 1, base 2 -> 1, base 3 -> 2, base 5 -> 3, base 6 -> 3.

scope question i cannot answer from the text and would want ruled: 'cards you control' plainly covers his action cards, but it also literally covers EQUIPMENT and WEAPONS he controls, which have {d} and {p} too. halving his equipment defence as well is a big further nerf and i do not want to assume it - the card database carries no reminder text for this, so per the golden rule this needs a human ruling before anyone builds it. same question for tokens he creates (might tokens etc).

engine-wise the natural home is the same place effCost / boardRed already sit: a base-stat reader that takes the card AND the side, so 'cards YOU control' is answered by whose side is asking. do it there once rather than at each call site, or the halving will get missed on exactly the paths nobody remembered - which is how it got missed in the first place.
